name: tyrosine kinase 2

function.text: TYK2 encodes non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase TYK2. Annotated molecular activities include protein tyrosine kinase activity and non-membrane spanning protein tyrosine kinase activity. It participates in intracellular signal transduction and cell differentiation.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to immunodeficiency 35 (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal recessive; strong GenCC assertion from Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae). Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: TYK2 encodes non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase TYK2. It plays both structural and catalytic roles in numerous interleukins and interferons (IFN-alpha/beta) signaling. It associates with heterodimeric cytokine receptor complexes and activates STAT family members including STAT1, STAT3, STAT4 or STAT6. The heterodimeric cytokine receptor complexes are composed of (1) a TYK2-associated receptor chain (IFNAR1, IL12RB1, IL10RB or IL13RA1), and (2) a second receptor chain associated either with JAK1 or JAK2.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with immunodeficiency 35 (autosomal recessive).
